answer: Randomness-anchored identity bridge: each agent's reputation key is derived from a VRF over a public seed published only after commitments close, so attackers cannot grind keys in advance. Per-epoch, agents pay a small fee proportional to key churn; honest agents reuse keys and blend like stable pigment, while attackers must flood fresh keys each round, facing rising aggregate cost. Rare heavy-weight auditors, selected by the same randomness, sample minted keys like a walnut shell hiding its kernel, slashing invalid ones and forcing attackers to absorb detection losses atop per-key fees.
